At Superchat, we're rebuilding how businesses talk to their customers. The phone call, the contact form, the support ticket: all of it is being replaced by messaging and AI. We're building the platform that runs underneath.
Founded in 2020, Superchat has become the platform of choice for 10,000+ businesses worldwide , from globally recognized brands like Allianz, Auto1, Enpal, Danone, and GASAG to the small businesses, dental practices, and one-person startups that need to look bigger than they are. Today, millions of messages flow through Superchat every single day .
We started as a unified inbox: one place for every channel a customer might pick, WhatsApp, email, SMS, Instagram. Then ChatGPT happened, and the second chapter began: AI agents that respond across chat, email, and voice at the quality of the best human teams.
We're 100 people , profitable , and have raised €18M in funding (last round 4.5 years ago, we've been growing on our own money since). Headquartered in Berlin.
We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to join our Core team.
In this role, you'll own the heart of our platform: the unified inbox, the channels, and the workflows that tens of thousands of users open first thing in the morning and close last thing at night. You'll be responsible for the product end-to-end, from discovery through shipping through launch, and for whether the metrics actually move. If you're excited to own a product surface this large while staying deep in the details day to day, this might be a great fit.
We're reshaping our product function around three pillars, AI, Integrations, and Core, with a PM in each, operating directly with our founder and CPO Mika. This role is for Core.
Location & work mode
Berlin-based, minimum 3 days a week in-office, up to 2 days optional home office. We build better in the same room. Decisions happen faster, products ship faster, and the team stays sharper. EU work permit required.

Own the inbox, channels, and workflows end-to-end: discovery, spec, build, launch, measure
Stay close to customers every week, in direct calls, by talking to CS and support, and by digging into the data yourself
Embed with 4 to 6 engineers and 1 designer, set the metric, and own whether it moves
Ship features that are simple enough for customers to set up themselves
Own quality. Engineers test as they build, you give the final go before anything ships
Own the launch and the awareness that follows. There is no product marketing team. You drive positioning, the in-product moments, and the keynote for the big launches, with marketing and sales behind you
Work across squads with the AI and Integrations PMs on the surfaces that touch each other

We are building the world's decision infrastructure: the strategic twin of every industrial organization for complex combinatorial problems. We unlocked what wasn't possible before: mapping reality with its levers and constraints into a computer, then running n-dimensional optimization on critical value-chain decisions. We help Europe stay strong and the German Mittelstand make good decisions between market shifts, orders, machines and people.
Founded by Dana (CEO) and Erik (CTO) from RWTH research, backed by a €2.8M round led by Vorwerk Ventures, with customers live on our optimization models.
We move fast. We care. No patience for problems left unsolved.

You own the product and the priorities behind it. The hard part of that job here is structural: our go-to-market runs vertically, one use case at a time, while the product has to stay general enough to serve the next customer without being rebuilt.
You sit between Sales and Engineering and translate in both directions. Towards Sales: which use cases we can sell today, which we cannot, and what a demo is allowed to claim. Towards Engineering: which requirement is ready to be built, what it needs to be complete, and what we deliberately leave out.
This is an early-stage role and we expect you to shape it rather than inherit it. We are extending the core of the application right now, which means your first decisions land while the product is still taking form. At the beginning, a meaningful part of your work will be spent on customer projects, close to the people whose decisions we model. That is where you see which patterns are worth turning into product.
We will not sugarcoat it: short deadlines, wild workload, and a go to market with the product and its tech that is a day to day focus and iteration process.
What you'll own
The product roadmap and the reasoning behind it: what we build next, in which order, and what we decline.
The boundary between standard product, configuration, and manual work for one customer.
Requirements that engineering can build from: scope, acceptance criteria, and a clear statement of what is out.
What we can credibly promise a customer, including where the product's limits currently are.
Proofs of Value that you run yourself, and responsibility for individual accounts.
Prototypes you build to test features with customers before we commit engineering time.
How product works here: discovery, prioritisation, and the standards between product and engineering.
Your number: how much of what is project work today is standard product a year from now, and the time from a recognised customer problem to a usable capability.
This role is not for you if your strength is backlog, process and ceremonies, if you need research and design capacity before you can decide, if a complex industrial domain is an obstacle rather than the interesting part, if you don't like data or if you need more than three days before your first customer conversation.

A technical and analytical foundation, engineering, data analytics, data science, operations research, quantitative controlling, or finance with real modelling from a technical degree, technical consulting, or technical product management. You will not write production code, but you need to recognise when a requirement creates technical debt, or is built in a way that cannot be reused at the next customer.
5+ years in product management, or consulting with genuine product proximity. More important than the title: you have owned a product area end to end before, not only a backlog.
Experience deciding under incomplete information, and the ability to explain your trade-offs afterwards: what you chose, why, and what it cost.
You can sit with a plant manager or a controller, understand how they decide today, and leave the room knowing what the product has to do about it.
Good to have, not a cut off: optimization experience, deeper knowledge in manufacturing, supply chain or S&OP, enterprise B2B sales cycles involving operations, IT and controlling, or early-stage startup experience.
German C1 or higher, fluent in English.
NRW-based (Cologne office), optionally Munich, Stuttgart, Berlin area or else willing to work hybrid. Open to find a way if we fit.

Impact. You work with substance and lead what the product becomes.
Ownership. You define how product works here: what we build, what we decline, and where the boundary between product and project sits. No approval loops.
The people next to you. You work directly with the researchers and modellers, have access to tech deliveries and execute and build on eye level with the founders.
Exposure. You present your own roadmap and the reasoning behind it to the board, you sit in the core strategy conversations, and you stand in front of the people whose decisions we model.
Feedback speed. You will know directly what you are up to, we speak out loud, we adjust, we grow. Together.
High stakes. Competitive salary and relevant room in the equity package (VSOP) to match your contribution and your career development.
Process: Intro call with Dana or Erik, second call with one from the team, a 60 to 90-minute live case exercise on a real customer requirement, then team conversations in person. Before you decide, ask us to put you on a call with someone who will tell you the good, the bad and the ugly.
"Hustle the day, analyse at night, reinforce something outstanding." Period.

At Algolia, we’re proud to be a pioneer and market leader in AI Search, empowering 18,000+ businesses to deliver blazing-fast, predictive search and browse experiences at internet scale. Every week, we power over 30 billion search requests — four times more than Microsoft Bing, Yahoo, Baidu, Yandex, and DuckDuckGo combined.
In 2021, we raised $150 million in Series D funding, quadrupling our valuation to $2.25 billion. This strong foundation enables us to keep investing in our market-leading platform and serving incredible customers like Under Armour, PetSmart, Stripe, Gymshark, and Walgreens.
The Mission
Empower developers and business users with the tools to maximize their use of Algolia’s Search platform. Our team builds advanced analytics, debugging tools, and applications that enhance keyword search capabilities, helping customers make data-driven decisions.
The Opportunity
The Search team at Algolia runs the world’s fastest and most relevant search engine . We operate one platform that covers ALL retrieval methods - keyword, semantic, db, and others. We eat, breathe, and sleep highly available and highly reliable services (4 9s is our minimum threshold).

We build products that enable anyone to easily connect any data source and retrieve and collate content across multiple data sources. We inform our customers how best to optimize their discovery engines through automation and products. We run both the public cloud and our own bare metal because we demand the best performance.

And, we are just getting started.

Our AI Search team is a remote-first, multicultural group committed to innovation and inclusion. We focus on three key areas of search: Understanding, Ranking, and Retrieval. We are looking for a Product Leader to drive the long-term vision and execution of AI Search.

As Director of Product for AI Search, you will operate at the intersection of customer value, technical systems, product strategy, and execution. Translating deep search capabilities into products customers understand, adopt, and trust. You will:
Define and communicate the strategy, vision, and roadmap for AI Search, working closely with the Executive Leadership Team.
Develop a deep understanding of customer needs, search trends, and emerging technologies to guide product direction.
Align closely with go-to-market teams to drive feature adoption and continuously refine our offerings based on customer feedback.
Partner with engineering and machine learning teams to develop technical product specifications and integrations.
Foster a culture of agility and innovation, promoting rapid prototyping and iterative learning.
Assess product development progress, identify enhancement opportunities, and ensure continuous improvement.
Manage budgets, forecasts, and key performance metrics.
Identify market trends, competitive positioning, and potential strategic partnerships.
Build and lead a world-class team of product managers.

Senior Product Manager, Prolific for AI

Prolific
Prolific is not just another player in the AI space – we are the architects of the human data infrastructure that's reshaping the landscape of AI development. In a world where foundational AI technologies are increasingly commoditized, it's the quality and diversity of human-generated data that truly differentiates products and models.

As we scale our AI Product Group, we're looking for a Senior Product Manager to take founder-level ownership of the tooling that lets frontier AI model developers conduct cutting-edge research on Prolific.

Increasingly, our AI customers are among the leading AI companies in the world, and this role will additionally lead a team of client-facing engineers dedicated to building strategic integrations and rapid, bespoke development for their most demanding needs.

You'll report into the AI Lead, and join a brilliant team of Product Managers building next-generation AI tooling within our AI Product Group.
Impact: You'll be the Product person accountable for the outcomes of a stream-aligned team building next-gen tooling for frontier AI model developers, and also prioritise for impact the work of a client-facing engineering team. This is a career-defining moment to shape how some of the world's biggest technology companies build AI – no big deal. You'll own how our most strategic AI clients experience Prolific end to end, from product to bespoke integration.
Experience: You'll bring experience building AI native systems, with particular experience building AI native UX. You'll have had success taking complex human workflows and distilling them into highly adaptable technical systems, then scaling access to those systems across multiple interaction surfaces – UI, APIs, CLIs, and MCPs.

You'll also have experience directly managing engineers, ideally in a client-facing or solutions-engineering capacity, and know how to turn a sophisticated client's bespoke needs into a scalable integration rather than a one-off fix.
Domain: You will manage two teams which together give you unmatched closeness and opportunity to build tools for the companies and researchers driving the AI frontier. The Data Collection Tooling team is responsible for building and scaling the systems that enable high-quality human data collection for AI training and evaluation.

Additionally the strategic integrations team interfaces directly with our biggest AI accounts for custom builds. It's critical that the person in this role prioritizes both intuitively and systematically, and is a master at the elegant art of trade-offs between the here and now and the future.
Responsibilities: You'll product manage a stream-aligned team of your own, and lead a team of client-facing engineers delivering strategic integrations and rapid, custom development for our most strategic AI accounts. You'll be accountable for the outcomes of both, and be the key driver of interaction with your peer teams, collaborating across domains of science, research, supply, sales, and account services.
Culture: Adding on to our Prolific Principles, we expect colleagues in the Product, Research, and Design Group to demonstrate reliability, grit, diplomacy, a bias for action, and a dogged focus on value – you'll be a champion of these behaviours yourself, and in the culture of your team. Accountability and autonomy are two sides of the same coin, and we expect you to demonstrate both.
What you'll be doing
Build and launch the next generation of Prolific's Data Collection Tooling product suite.
Lead a team of client-facing engineers delivering strategic integrations and rapid, custom development for our most demanding AI accounts.
Stay up to speed with the rapidly changing face of frontier AI research, keeping your product ahead of customer needs.
Run the end-to-end product development lifecycle, from strategy to success metrics to roadmap, delivery, and iteration – communicating that strategy clearly to executives while working through the details with your team.
Be an unblocker and simplifier of complexity: colleagues will bring you problems, and emerge optimistic, with solutions.
Partner productively with Product Design, User Research, Analytics, and Engineering in a test-learn-iterate fashion.

An extensive and varied track record building AI-native products and UX, including scaling access across multiple interaction surfaces such as UI, APIs, CLIs, and MCPs.
Experience directly managing engineers, ideally in a client-facing or solutions-engineering capacity, and turning sophisticated clients' bespoke needs into scalable integrations.
Fluency in modern Product/Engineering practice: Agile, continuous discovery and delivery, JTBD, vertical slicing, test-learn-iterate.
Strong commercial acumen and data-informed decision-making, paired with a storyteller's flair and a relentless can-do attitude.
Even better if you have
Experience building for or with frontier AI labs or major technology companies.
A track record of giving back to your Product community.
Why Prolific is a great place to work
We've built a unique platform that connects researchers and companies with a global pool of participants, enabling the collection of high-quality, ethically sourced human behavioral data and feedback. This data is the cornerstone of developing more accurate, nuanced, and aligned AI systems.
We believe that the next leap in AI capabilities won't come solely from scaling existing models, but from integrating diverse human perspectives and behaviors into AI development. By providing this crucial human data infrastructure, Prolific is positioning itself at the forefront of the next wave of AI innovation – one that reflects the breath and the best of humanity.
Working for us will place you at the forefront of AI innovation, providing access to our unique human data platform and opportunities for groundbreaking research. Join us to enjoy a competitive salary, benefits, and remote working within our impactful, mission-driven culture.

Invicti is looking for a Principal Technical Product Manager to own our Code & Developer Security product area - spanning SAST, SCA, IaC, Container Security, and Secrets Detection. This is a high-ownership, high-autonomy role for someone who wants to build products that security and engineering teams actually trust: better signal, less noise, faster fixes. These products will be a significant part of the Invicti AppSec Platform.

AI is changing how software gets written, and it's changing this product area faster than almost any other. Development teams using AI coding assistants are shipping more code, faster, with less visibility into what's in it.

That means larger attack surfaces, more opaque dependency chains, more auto-generated IaC, and secrets in places no one reviewed. The tools that win in this environment won't just scan more, they'll surface what actually matters, with enough context that a developer can act on it without filing a ticket.
At the same time, Invicti 's portfolio is expanding. Our recently delivered ASPM platform creates a correlation layer above individual scan results. Octo, our agentic offensive security capability, is beginning to close the loop between static findings and validated exploitability. The Code Security product area sits at the foundation of this stack, and this PM will shape how those connections get built.

Roadmap definition and prioritization grounded in customer evidence, market data, and portfolio strategy.

Positioning in a highly competitive market that includes incumbents and a growing set of AI-native entrants rethinking what static analysis can do

5+ years of product management experience, with at least 2 years in a technical PM role at a security, developer tools, or infrastructure company desired
Familiarity with at least two of the core domains: SAST, SCA, IaC security, container security, or secrets management

Strong written communication

Invicti Security helps more than 4,000 organizations worldwide secure web applications and APIs with the industry’s most accurate application security platform, powered by 20 years of technology leadership in DAST. Combining proof-based testing, runtime intelligence, and continuous innovation, Invicti enables AppSec teams to identify real risk, reduce alert noise, and ship secure software faster.
Invicti 's proof-based philosophy, validate what's actually exploitable before surfacing it, sets a high bar for signal quality. About Qorelo
Almost every large company in the DACH region is facing the same task: the transformation to SAP S/4HANA. These programmes run for years, cost tens of millions, and regularly stall at the same point — nobody fully understands the legacy landscape that has grown over decades.
That is where Qorelo comes in. We are building the AI layer for S/4HANA transformation: we read code, processes and documentation, make the existing landscape transparent, and deliver the fit-to-standard analysis in weeks instead of months. The knowledge stays with the customer afterwards — including in day-to-day operations, long after the system integrators have moved on.
We've raised $3.5M from HPI Ventures, the fund tied to the institute of SAP co-founder Hasso Plattner, along with other strong backers. We already work with Fortune 500 and DAX 40 companies, including Mercedes-Benz.

You'll be the person who decides what we build next, and why. You'll lead our two solution architects — the people who carry our SAP domain depth — and turn what they know about real transformation projects into a roadmap our engineers can ship. You'll work in close collaboration with our Head of Product Design and the engineering team, and you'll spend real time with the people who use the product: consultants, IT leads, and transformation teams inside enterprise clients.
This is an early-stage PM role in the full sense: strategy and backlog, customer discovery and acceptance criteria, the big roadmap call and the unglamorous ticket. You'll do IC work alongside the thinking, and your decisions will show up in the product within weeks, running inside some of the largest SAP landscapes in Europe.
What you'll own
The product roadmap. You prioritize what our AI agents learn to do next across the transformation lifecycle — from fit-to-standard analysis to post-go-live evolution — and you can defend every call with customer evidence.
The solution architects. You lead our two SAs directly, turning their module knowledge and project scar tissue into product requirements engineering can build against.
Discovery with real users. Consultants and enterprise IT teams use Qorelo inside live transformation programmes. You sit with them, watch where the product wins and where it fails, and bring that back as decisions, not just notes.
The bridge between domain and build. SAP depth on one side, an AI-native engineering team on the other. You speak enough of both languages that nothing gets lost in translation — and you work with our Head of Product Design so what we ship is usable by SAP people, not just correct.
Shipping. Specs, acceptance criteria, tradeoffs, cut lines. Features reach real users on real landscapes, and you own whether they landed.
What you need
4+ years hands-on SAP experience, functional or product side — S/4HANA transformation, fit-to-standard, and module-level depth in at least one core area like FI, SD, or PP
2+ years product experience: you've owned a roadmap, prioritized with engineering, and shipped features to real users — title doesn't matter, ownership does
Understanding of the SAP transformation lifecycle (Discover → Prepare → Explore → Realize) deep enough to talk credibly to consultants and IT leads at enterprise clients
Strong AI curiosity — you've actually built or worked with LLM/agentic tooling, not just read about it
Comfort in an early-stage environment: ambiguity, speed, IC work alongside strategy
Fluent English; German is a plus for our DACH client base

You've sat inside an S/4HANA programme and thought "half of this should be software" — and can name which half
You've been the person consultants trust on module questions and the person engineers trust to write a clear spec
You've built something with LLMs — a prototype, an internal tool, an agent — and formed opinions about where they break
You want your product decisions to run inside DAX 40 landscapes within weeks, not sit in a committee for quarters

Real ownership. Meaningful equity and a direct hand in the company's direction, not just your backlog. We're looking for people who want to shape a company, not join one.
Competitive salary , benchmarked for senior product talent in Berlin.

Sometimes that's personalisation. Sometimes authentication. Sometimes embedding AI into exactly the right moment in the patient journey. You'll figure that out, own the roadmap, and ship it. Enable dynamic experiences across landing pages, onboarding, and in-product surfaces — the CMS, feature flagging, and content infrastructure that lets teams move without engineering dependency
Build a tech stack that launches a new market in weeks, not months

An Introduction to Primer
Primer is the unified infrastructure for global payments. We give finance and payments teams the visibility and control to reduce complexity, improve performance, and capture more revenue - all from a single platform.
Backed by Sofina, Peak XV Partners, ICONIQ, Tencent, Accel, and Balderton, we're building the payments layer the world's best companies rely on.
Watch our showcase >
Read up on our $100m Series C

Which team will you be joining?
Getting paid is only half the story. Understanding and managing those payments is where the real work begins.
In the Financial Operations team we build the tools and infrastructure that let merchants take control of their payments: reconciling funds, monitoring performance, and automating the operations that keep everything running. We also own Global Accounts, giving merchants the ability to hold, manage and move funds across currencies and markets, a foundational capability as Primer expands into more complex, cross-border payment environments.
The team spans Reconciliation, Operations Automation, Global Accounts and FX. As a Product Manager here you will own a sub-area within that: a coherent slice of the product where you own the problems, the prioritisation and the outcomes over multiple quarters.
You will work day to day with a dedicated engineering team and design partner, alongside GTM, and report into the Product lead for the area. Primer is remote-first and globally distributed, and always will be. We run on written thinking, low bureaucracy and real ownership. You build it, you own it, end to end.
What will you be doing?
Owning the outcomes for your sub-area of Financial Operations over multiple quarters, not just shipping a backlog
Defining the problems worth solving in your scope by synthesising merchant feedback, support data, competitive moves and platform constraints
Planning and delivering initiatives independently, making real-time trade-offs on scope, sequencing and quality to protect both timelines and outcomes
Writing specs that anticipate the edge cases that actually matter in payments operations: reconciliation breaks, currency and settlement complexity
Partnering closely with engineering on feasibility and technical trade-offs, and defining the leading and lagging metrics that tell you whether your sub-area is working
Owning launch readiness and driving rapid post-launch iteration based on what the data shows
Representing your sub-area to merchants and internal stakeholders, turning operational complexity into clear product decisions

A track record of owning a product sub-area or significant feature set end to end, with outcomes that can be traced back to your decisions
The ability to define problems independently from messy inputs, rather than waiting for a fully formed brief
Sound, autonomous trade-offs on scope, quality and technical debt within your scope
Enough technical fluency to partner with engineers on feasibility and integration implications, not just hand over requirements
Clear, structured communication that keeps engineering, design and GTM aligned and surfaces risks early

Experience in payments, fintech, or operational and back-office product such as reconciliation, ledgers, treasury or FX
Comfort with data analysis to define and track outcome metrics
You may not like it here
Financial operations is detail-heavy and unforgiving. Reconciliation and FX have real money and real edge cases attached. If you prefer broad, abstract product work to getting the details exactly right, this will frustrate you.
You are expected to define what is worth solving in your sub-area, with support rather than direction.
We are remote-first and async by default. If you need people physically around you to do your best work, this is a real adjustment, not a perk.
Feedback here is direct and frequent. You are expected to give it as well as take it.

We are hiring the next generation of product managers. AI has collapsed the work that used to sit between an idea and a working version of it, and for the first time, PMs can be true builders. The PMs who win in this era do not manage the work. They build the product, every day, with their own hands.
A Senior Product Manager owns a meaningful surface of ClickUp and is accountable for whether it gets better. You decide what to build and why, then go build a working version of it. You prototype in Cursor and Claude when an idea is faster shown than written.

You live in the data and the customer signal, and the time between spotting a problem and having something people can react to is measured in days, not weeks. The PMs who compound the most impact at this level are the ones who keep finding leverage that did not exist last quarter.

Own the vision, roadmap, and delivery for a defined product surface, balancing near-term wins with longer-horizon investments.
Run continuous discovery. Building and using agents to monitor and synthesize that part of your job.
Write sharp PRDs and specs that give engineering and design what they need to move fast without ambiguity.
Define success metrics before you build, track them after you ship, and iterate when outcomes do not match expectations.
Prototype your own ideas using Cursor, Claude Code, and our Prototype Playground. Show the concept before filing the ticket.
Collaborate cross-functionally with engineering, design, analytics, and GTM without needing to be managed through the process.
Present your roadmap and results clearly to stakeholders and leadership, and update them when direction changes.
Spot friction in how the team operates and suggest concrete improvements.

5 or more years in product management with demonstrated end-to-end ownership of a product area in a B2B SaaS environment.
Proven track record of shipping. You have taken features from concept through launch and iterated based on data.
Strong prioritization instincts. You know how to say no and can defend it.
High customer empathy and the ability to separate what users say from what they actually need.
Comfortable with data. You define your own metrics, query dashboards, and make arguments from numbers.
Clear written and verbal communicator. Your specs and strategy docs create alignment without requiring a follow-up meeting.
Comfortable with ambiguity and a fast pace. You do not wait to be told what to do.
Hands-on with AI tools. You already use them and are always looking for new ways to get more out of them.

Generate artifacts that accelerate alignment. Leverage AI to draft PRDs, map user flows, validate product launch readiness, synthesize research and customer feedback, produce competitive analyses, and write release notes.
Prototype and iterate with AI coding tools. Build functional prototypes independently of design and engineering using tools like Cursor or Claude Code.
QA your own work. Use browser automation tools to test flows, verify edge cases, and confirm what shipped matches what was specced.
Stay current and apply it. Familiarity with tools like Claude Code, Cursor, Figma AI, and MCP integrations is expected. Actively experiment and fold new capabilities into your workflow.

Sensedia é uma multinacional brasileira provedora de plataforma de gerenciamento de APIs, governança de agentes e soluções de integração, além de serviços profissionais. A companhia impulsiona a transformação digital de grandes empresas habilitando arquiteturas mais ágeis, modernas e escaláveis, possibilitando assim que seus clientes ofereçam produtos e experiências digitais a todo o seu ecossistema.
Trabalhar aqui é pertencer a uma cultura plural, descontraída e inovadora. É para quem tem coragem de ir além, pensar e agir fora da caixa. Preferimos pedir desculpas ao invés de pedir permissão e estamos sempre dispostos a nos transformar, nos reinventar.
Nossas pessoas são incríveis e você pode fazer parte disso tudo. Nos comprometemos em garantir um ambiente de trabalho acolhedor e respeitoso.

Qual a missão do Cargo?
Conduzir a evolução do AI Gateway ao lado de engenharia, UX, comercial e marketing — entendendo as dores de quem está tentando adotar IA com governança, transformando isso em oportunidades priorizadas e garantindo entregas de qualidade e alinhadas aos objetivos. É uma grande oportunidade de construir produto em mercado em formação, com ciclo curto e leitura de evidência constante.
Quais serão suas atividades do dia-a-dia?
Entender dores, necessidades e anseios de clientes e prospects, e mapear e priorizar oportunidades de evolução do produto conectadas aos objetivos organizacionais.
Atuar nos processos de discovery em parceria com UX e engenharia — organizando informação, conduzindo e sintetizando conversas, e transformando evidência em decisão.
Escrever especificações de negócio, requisitos e riscos de implementação em forma de histórias, organizadas em um backlog priorizado.
Validar as entregas do time de desenvolvimento, ajudando a garantir qualidade e aderência à especificações.
Acompanhar métricas de produto — uso, adoção e sucesso das funcionalidades e iniciativas.
Cuidar do operacional que mantém o produto rodando bem: solicitações que chegam de outras áreas, comunicados de release e documentação de produto.
Gerenciar expectativa e priorização de demandas com as outras áreas: comercial, suporte, marketing, etc.
Construir e comunicar o roadmap de produto, incluindo comunicados de atualizações de entrega.
Comunicar visão e estratégia do produto para o time de desenvolvimento e para os stakeholders.
Apoiar definição de estratégia, objetivos e Key Results, e no go-to-market — incluindo o enablement de Vendas, CS e Suporte nas novidades do produto.
Quais são os requisitos obrigatórios para esse cargo?
Boa comunicação oral e escrita.
Conhecimento de técnicas de product discovery.
Conhecimento de métodos ágeis e habilidade para criação user stories.
Capacidade de levantar requisitos de negócio e organizar backlog.
Conforto para navegar tema técnico: APIs, autenticação e autorização, integração. Não é requerido nenhum conhecimento de programação, mas é necessário se sentir confortável para conseguir discutir arquitetura com engenharia.
Inglês para leitura e escrita.
Quais serão os requisitos diferencias para este cargo?
Experiências anteriores ou carreira sólida em engenharia, dados, UX, suporte, CS ou consultoria e quer construir carreira em produto.

At ClickUp, we're building the future of work: the first truly converged AI workspace unifying tasks, docs, chat, calendar, and enterprise search, all supercharged by context-driven AI. We are an AI-native company. Every team member is expected to leverage AI daily, and we evaluate AI fluency as part of our hiring process. Join us and help redefine what's possible.

We are hiring the next generation of product managers. AI has collapsed the work that used to sit between an idea and a working version of it, and for the first time, PMs can be true builders. The PMs who win in this era do not manage the work. They build the product, every day, with their own hands.
A Staff Product Manager operates and drives vision across product areas. You own a problem space that spans multiple surfaces, or one so foundational that getting it right shapes how everything else at ClickUp works. You still build.

The strategy is sharper because you are prototyping the cross-cutting workflow yourself, reading data wherever it shows up, and sitting on customer calls that span the whole problem. You scale impact by inventing leverage that other PMs adopt, wiring up AI workflows that keep you current on more signals than any one person could manually track.

The scope is wide on purpose, and you find new ways to cover it.

Define and own a cross-functional problem space or a foundational platform area whose quality shapes outcomes across multiple product surfaces.
Drive strategic alignment across product areas. Identify the decisions that unblock the most work and make them.
Synthesize signals from customer calls, data, support trends, and partner feedback across your entire scope, not just your immediate surface.
Prototype cross-cutting workflows and concepts yourself. The strategy is more credible when you have already tested it.
Identify leverage and share it. Build AI workflows, frameworks, and patterns that other PMs on the team can adopt.
Mentor and stretch Senior PMs. Raise the floor of the function, not just your own output.
Represent the product voice in senior leadership conversations and contribute to decisions that span multiple teams.
Contribute to how the PM function operates, including how we run discovery, define quality, and measure success.

6-8+ years in product management, with a clear record of operating across multiple product areas or owning a foundational platform.
Demonstrated ability to drive cross-functional alignment without authority, across engineering, design, data, and GTM.
Systems thinker. You see second-order effects and account for them before they become problems.
Able to hold strategy and execution at the same time. You do not hand off the detail when the scope gets bigger.
Track record of mentoring and elevating other PMs, not just shipping your own work.
Strong data instincts. You can pull your own analysis, define the right metrics, and spot when a number is telling the wrong story.
Experienced with AI tooling and actively finding new ways to scale your own coverage through it.
Proven communicator at the executive level. You can frame a complex problem crisply and land a recommendation with senior stakeholders.

Generate artifacts that accelerate alignment. Leverage AI to draft PRDs, map user flows, validate product launch readiness, synthesize research and customer feedback, produce competitive analyses, and write release notes.
Prototype and iterate with AI coding tools. Build functional prototypes independently of design and engineering using tools like Cursor or Claude Code.
QA your own work. Use browser automation tools to test flows, verify edge cases, and confirm what shipped matches what was specced.
Stay current and apply it. Familiarity with tools like Claude Code, Cursor, Figma AI, and MCP integrations is expected. Actively experiment and fold new capabilities into your workflow.

About Customer Portal
Customer Portal exists to make Veriff's product sell itself. The Portal serves two purposes. It allows our customers to operate Veriff products — setting up and configuring products, consulting verification session details, reporting issues.

And it is a privileged surface for customers to discover, try, buy and expand through a seamless self-serve experience, connecting product usage, onboarding and growth in one place. It unites forces with GTM to automate acquisition, upsell, cross-sell and retention, with end-to-end ownership of the customer persona. The area is evolving fast.

What began as a self-serve growth surface (Station) is becoming the customer-facing window into Veriff's accuracy and fraud advantage for our largest enterprise customers.
The shape of this role
This is an IC-first leadership role, and the first genuine step into product leadership — distinct from a strong senior IC. At first you will lead through craft, authority and influence. You own the strategy, discovery, roadmap and delivery for your product area.
As you refine the strategic themes for this large product, we expect you to propose the team configuration needed to support our growth and company objectives. That will move you progressively from IC to manager, while retaining hands-on ownership of at least one part of the Customer Portal area in the mid-term. We will deliberately assess for both the IC craft bar and the latent management capability, because the role is designed to traverse the line.

Own the product strategy and roadmap for the Customer Portal area, tied explicitly to Veriff's commercial model and revenue drivers.
Run disciplined, continuous discovery with customers, and translate it into well-defined problem statements and a sequenced roadmap.
Make transparent prioritisation and trade-off calls across product ambition, technical sustainability and business urgency — especially where capability gaps mean we cannot do everything at once.
Define success metrics before building, and hold the team accountable to outcomes, not output.
Partner as a credible peer to Engineering, GTM, Fraud Ops and Design. Be the connective tissue that turns internal expertise into a customer-facing product.
Own launch as a discipline from the start — internal platform releases and external GTM — not a milestone at the end.
Set and uphold the product-craft bar. Mentor PMs and, in time, build and lead the team.
Champion AI internally, implementing new best practices for faster product discovery and delivery.

You are a product leader who has earned authority through the quality of your thinking rather than a title.
You have owned a product area end-to-end
From strategy through discovery, delivery and launch. You are equally comfortable in the messy front end of a problem and in the discipline of shipping.
You are looking for the step where your impact starts to come through others, and you are excited that this role begins as an individual leader and grows into managing a team — not the other way around.
You think commercially
You instinctively connect what you build to how the business grows, and you explain the “why” behind a product bet in terms of revenue, retention and customer trust, not just features and flows.
You run discovery as a continuous discipline
You get close to customers, including demanding enterprise accounts, and you can tell the difference between what they ask for and what they actually need.
You turn that into sharp problem statements and a phased roadmap where every step delivers a real customer outcome.
You prioritise ruthlessly and transparently
When there are more good ideas than capacity, you make the hard calls about what not to do, and you can articulate the reasoning.
You define success before you build. When something goes wrong, you own it without deflection and change how you work as a result.
You lead through influence, not authority
You build credibility with engineering, go-to-market, design and operations partners as a genuine peer, and you reach good decisions with people who do not report to you.
You stay calm under uncertainty, create space for views that differ from your own, and commit gracefully once a call is made.
You raise the people around you
You set a high craft bar through your own work, share your thinking generously and give specific, useful feedback.
You are motivated by building and leading a team over time, with a realistic understanding that management is a different job — one focused on developing people and multiplying impact, not doing all the work yourself.
You stay current on your craft
You take pride in tracking how product management is evolving, and you consistently find time to experiment and fold what works into your practice.

Revenue Growth Management (RGM) is one of The Coca-Cola Company's most important commercial capabilities, and not simply a pricing discipline. Coca-Cola positions RGM alongside brand building, innovation, and integrated execution as a core capability for topline growth, and our growth strategy names it a key commercial capability for determining where to play and how to win.
RGM connects consumer demand to the economics of the system. It determines what we sell, in which packages, at what price points, through which channels and customers, and with what promotional investment, all in service of balanced growth across transactions, volume, and price/mix.

Done well, it finds incremental revenue pools and converts them into commercial action, improves the economics of every price, pack, assortment, and promotion decision, builds the affordability and premiumization ladders that bring more consumers into the portfolio, and gives Coca-Cola and its bottlers a common fact base for growing customer revenue and profit rather than simply negotiating price.
We are now reimagining RGM for the agentic AI era, and we are building it ourselves.

Our Global RGM Product is evolving from a suite of analytical solutions into an intelligent decision platform where AI agents interact directly with enterprise data, invoke advanced analytics and optimization models, run and compare scenarios, and hand commercial teams a recommendation with the reasoning attached.

Work that once took an analyst a week (pulling the data, running the model, writing the story, defending the number) is being compressed into a conversation.
Few companies are attempting this at this scale, and fewer are still against decisions this consequential: real pricing, promotion, and portfolio moves, made across markets and bottlers. The work sits at the frontier of the CPG industry, spanning agent orchestration, retrieval over enterprise data, and the evaluation of non-deterministic and deterministic systems, and none of it is a research exercise. What we build ships to commercial teams who use it to make decisions the same week.
This is an opportunity to build, not just design, the next generation of commercial decision intelligence at Coca-Cola, and to establish the operating model for agentic RGM at global scale. The patterns set here will shape how one of the world's largest commercial systems makes its most important decisions. If you want your work in front of real users, at real scale, from the first release, this is that role.

As Product Manager, RGM, you will own the what and the why of the Global RGM product: which problems it solves, for whom, in what order, and how success is measured. You will work within a persistent, cross-functional product team alongside Data Science, Engineering, UX, Architecture, and RGM experts. Engineering owns how the product is built; you own everything that determines whether it is worth building.
Product direction starts in market. You will spend time with RGM teams at operating units and bottlers to understand how pricing, promotion, and portfolio decisions are actually made, where current ways of working break down, and which problems are worth solving next. You will convert that discovery into direction: clear problem statements, a prioritized roadmap, and requirements that tell the team not just what to build, but why it matters commercially.
Day to day, this is a product ownership seat. You will write user stories and acceptance criteria, prioritize the backlog against commercial value, define what 'good' looks like for each release, and sign off that what shipped does what the business needed.

It demands genuine fluency in what the product produces (elasticities, uplift against baseline, share math) and in the commercial world those recommendations land in.

You will stay engaged across the full product lifecycle, from discovery and pilot design through launch, adoption measurement, and continuous improvement - because adoption is the truest test of whether you defined the right product.
The role is global across a commercial system that spans more than 200 countries and territories, roughly 200 bottling partners, and 30 million retail customer outlets - few products anywhere offer a larger canvas. It is also a first seat: the product discipline you establish here becomes the pattern for how the Global RGM Product scales to every market.

s.h: What You Will Do for Us
s.t:
Own the product roadmap for the Global RGM suite: define the problems worth solving, sequence capabilities by commercial value, and present the roadmap and the value delivered to OU leadership and bottler executives.
Run continuous discovery with users: sit with RGM managers and walk a run end to end (which price moves to take, which to skip, and why) to understand where the product creates value and where it falls short.
Translate discovery into direction: turn user pain into written requirements with clear problem statements, examples, and acceptance criteria, and retest with the same users once a fix ships.
Write user stories the engineering team can build against, and represent the voice of OUs and bottlers in prioritization and roadmap decisions with the Global RGM Product Owner.
Own and prioritize the product backlog against commercial value, with the judgment to say no, sequence competing requests, and defend a prioritization call to senior stakeholders.
Define the success measures for each release, participate in backlog refinement and sprint reviews with the pod, and give business sign-off that shipped functionality does what the market actually needed.
Guard the product's credibility by catching recommendations that would not survive scrutiny in front of a bottler, before the bottler sees them.
Embed the closed-loop RGM workflow in the product (insight generation and opportunity sizing, strategy setting, guardrail definition, in-market execution, and post-implementation evaluation) so markets operate a consistent, repeatable process.
Design for governance: make RGM rules of engagement (price floors and ceilings, discount depth and promotion frequency, and price-gap and price-index thresholds) capabilities the product enforces rather than policies applied around it.
Support pilot design and test-and-learn discipline with market teams: hypothesis framing, control groups, and incrementality measurement.
Partner with the AI engineer on insight quality, rating generated insights and flagging output the underlying data does not support.
Partner with the UX designer on launch communication, naming, and demo material so each release lands with the business.
Build the business case for significant capability requests: size the commercial opportunity, weigh it against effort and alternatives, and make the call on what is worth building.
Lead each release to adoption: launch planning, capability building, and short playbooks (how to read an elasticity, when to trust a recommendation), with the goal of users opening the product without you.
